folk.why:wayfinder: Sits down at any room made ready for a holder.
folk.why:provisioner: Hears when one of us carries more lees than our hearths use.
folk.why:smith: Word of an anvil brings her. Whoever works iron will want harder ore.
folk.why:apothecary: Wants Vanahar Remains while they are fresh, for a holder's dead hand.
folk.why:tinker: Has never seen two pieces joined, and our Joining Bench can do it.
folk.why:runescribe: Cuts lines in stone. Our Line Frame means crystal out of deep rock.
folk.why:beastcaller: Lives on Tama remains, which we can supply now that Kankāl is dead.
folk.why:deserter: Left by a beaten Sand March, too far from a fire to reach it by dark.
folk.meet:wayfinder: You have a door, a light and a bed, peopl. I hold here from tonight.
folk.meet:provisioner: They said on the road that you carry more lees than your hearths use, peopl. I carry meat, hide and coal.
folk.meet:smith: An anvil here means you will dig for harder ore, peopl. I can shape a bar of any metal you bring me.
folk.meet:apothecary: Vanahar's remains brought me, peopl, while they are fresh. I sell salves and see to holders' arms.
folk.meet:tinker: I came to see your Joining Bench, peopl. I have handled small pieces all my life and never seen two joined.
folk.meet:runescribe: Your Line Frame means someone here brings crystal out of deep rock, peopl. I cut lines in hearthstones.
folk.meet:beastcaller: Kankāl is dead, peopl, and Tama come in packs at every dusk. I bind their remains to bone for small ones.
folk.meet:deserter: I came with the march that was beaten here, peopl, and could not reach a fire by dark. I sell for Mūda.
folk.housed:wayfinder: They said every stone on this road was lit once.
The crates in the next old houses are empty. Put food in them if you pass that way.
Ask me which stone comes next. I know where each kind lies and how each offering is made.
Bedrolls and recall stones come out of the old houses. No one born here has a use for either.
If a nest has got into a Broken Store by the road, clear it before a walker sits down there.
Tell me whether the floor at the next stone is whole. I carry word of it to the other hearths.
folk.housed:provisioner: I buy anything, because somebody two hearths on will want it.
Take food with you when you go Under.
Two pots this close bring them at dusk. I told the others so before I sat down here.
The hearths that hunt ordinary animals sell me their meat and hide. What they want back is lees.
Bring me hide from Tusāravan. A holder's bed is hide over boards, and it wears through.
Coal sells in the cold country, if you have any to spare.
folk.housed:smith: Iron lifts with a stone pick. Hīrak needs an iron one.
I can shape a bar of any metal. From Jalit up I cannot make the bar.
A forge of remains against my wall draws, and I am the one sitting up beside it.
I have looked all my life for a forge of the forebears and never found a ring standing.
Bring me raw ore of a metal I have only seen poured.
If you get a tool whole out of a Sealed Store, let me see it before you use it.
folk.housed:apothecary: Put it on the table, away from the pot.
This is what a holder drinks at first light, and it does the same for your arm.
A second salve does nothing until the first has closed the wound.
An old holder's hand goes dead and sets, the way metal sets. The remains might loosen it.
It has not worked yet. I need more of the remains, and fresh.
Bring me any old salve you find in a Sealed Store.
folk.housed:tinker: The one who taught me had never joined two pieces either.
Two pieces that do the same thing do it no better worn together.
If you get into a Sealed Store, bring out the small things as well as the bars.
Hold a piece out to me and I can tell you which store it came from.
I know what a piece does by holding it.
The old pieces were made by hands with a skill that nobody has now, I think.
folk.housed:runescribe: A staff is the same work as a hearthstone, pointed away from you.
A bad cut leaks into the arm, and the arm tires sooner for the same work.
Where to cut is learned by the hand. I cannot tell it to you.
I held one of those recall stones all night once, and it did nothing for me.
Crystal grows in the dark rock. There is nothing of any kill in it.
At a great stone, look at the place for the hand. Tell me how many lines leave it.
folk.housed:beastcaller: It stays for what is on the bone.
Do not bring it inside my walls. Unsalted is food, and I sit beside a pot.
If you find a nest in the old stonework, tell me what kind was in it before you break it.
A second one will stay for the whistle. They come to the sound.
The other holders do not like my trade, because what I carry is food to feeders.
The eight at the stones are beasts, peopl, of the same kinds that come up at night, only larger.
folk.housed:deserter: I marched with them and I will not again.
A Mūda is a night inside the light at any fire of ours.
While the burrower lived nothing else came up on the sand.
Everything I sell, a march took from a store and could not burn.
The old at the fires say another burrower will come onto the sand if the stones there are left alone.
I know when a march will come and what it will go for.
folk.stage:wayfinder.1: Vanahar is dead, peopl. The telling says its country is taken back by that.
Kāru will come to a Joining Bench, and Vejja is already on the road for the remains.
folk.stage:wayfinder.2: Bed Maruhar's remains in a ring of Deep Rock and light a fire under them. That fire melts Jalit.
Kankāl comes next. Its offering is a bell, rung on its stone.
folk.stage:wayfinder.3: They are saying on the road that Kankāl lay on a seal, and you have broken it.
Its remains make the Hollow Gate. Under is open to you now.
folk.stage:wayfinder.4: Guhamāt's remains in a ring of Hollow Rock will work Tala.
Jīmūt is next. Its kite is flown from the stone.
folk.stage:wayfinder.5: Jīmūt's remains make the second gate.
The telling does not say where that gate goes, and none of us has been through it.
folk.stage:wayfinder.6: Work Patik in the Ratan Furnace, and make Kuranga's mask from it.
Kuranga comes up only after dark. The mask is worn at its stone at night.
folk.stage:wayfinder.7: Kuranga is dead. In a ring of Black Glass its remains will work Gahan.
Make the Cairn Key of Gahan. It opens the Cairn.
folk.stage:wayfinder.8: You opened the Cairn, peopl. The stones can be lit again.
A householder would have to sit at one of them through the night, and none of us has done that.
folk.stage:provisioner.1: Vanahar's remains, boiled down, are better lees than any pot on this road has had.
folk.stage:provisioner.2: The Maruhar Furnace still needs a fire under it. I sell coal.
folk.stage:provisioner.3: The road says you broke a seal under Kankāl, peopl. The nights are worse, and the hearths will want more lees.
folk.stage:provisioner.4: Brown caps from Under make a stew. Bring me some and I will carry them on.
folk.stage:provisioner.5: When you come back through the second gate, bring the fruit you find there. I can sell it.
folk.stage:provisioner.6: Kuranga comes up only at night, they say. Take meat and arrows enough for a night away from a hearth.
folk.stage:provisioner.7: Kuranga is dead, and the Cairn is all the telling has left. I have arrows and meat for the walk.
folk.stage:provisioner.8: Whatever came out of the Cairn, peopl, I will buy by weight like anything else.
folk.stage:smith.1: Vanahar was full of iron bars. Sell me the ones you do not need.
folk.stage:smith.2: I sell Jalit bars and Jalit arrows now. I can work a bar of it, and I could not make one.
A Jalit arrowhead burns what it goes into.
folk.stage:smith.3: The Hollow Gate is seven pieces of Black Glass round Kankāl's remains, fitted on an anvil.
folk.stage:smith.4: Guhamāt was full of Antar bars. I have them to sell now.
folk.stage:smith.5: Jīmūt gave up Tala bars. Where does Tala ore lie, peopl? I have never seen it in the rock.
folk.stage:smith.6: Patik comes out of the Ratan Furnace. I can shape it once you have it.
folk.stage:smith.7: Gahan is the hardest metal I know of. Bring me a bar from the Kuranga Furnace and I will shape it.
folk.stage:smith.8: The arms that came out of the Cairn are better made than mine. I want to see how they were worked.
folk.stage:apothecary.2: I tried Vanahar's remains on a dead hand again. It has not loosened.
folk.stage:apothecary.3: You can go Under now. Bring me what grows there and I can make the Greater Salve and the Greater Tonic.
folk.stage:apothecary.4: Lit caps from Under make a broth that eases the arm. Bring me more of them.
folk.stage:apothecary.5: The fruit from past the second gate closes a wound a little. Bring me one to try.
folk.stage:apothecary.6: My tonic is ground crystal in fruit juice. If the Ratan Crystal grinds finer, I want a piece.
folk.stage:apothecary.7: Kuranga's remains loosen the hardest ore. I would try a piece on a dead hand, if you can spare one.
folk.stage:apothecary.8: Nihān's remains are the strongest the stones have given. A piece of them might loosen a dead hand.
folk.stage:tinker.2: Kammār has Jalit now, so I can stock the Long Glove. There is a part of Jalit in it.
folk.stage:tinker.3: Let me hold the Kankāl Plate, peopl. It weighs more than any piece its size I have handled.
folk.stage:tinker.4: Posak says one more small one stays by a hand that wears the Guhamāt Cap. I have never had a piece like it.
folk.stage:tinker.5: Pieces of the same stuff as the Jīmūt Feather lie in old stores. It weighs almost nothing and bears weight.
folk.stage:tinker.6: Worn on the driving arm, the Ratan Crystal makes it tire slower. I can tell that by holding it.
folk.stage:tinker.7: Wear the Kuranga Tine and it loosens a little wherever you strike, so every blow goes in further.
folk.stage:tinker.8: The Cairn Gem is a piece of Dressed Stone with a gem set in it. I do not know the make.
folk.stage:runescribe.1: Was the hollow for the hand at Vanahar's stone worn smooth, peopl? Long holding wears it.
folk.stage:runescribe.2: Maruhar's stone sits in a bowl of sand. Was its housing cut the way Vanahar's was?
folk.stage:runescribe.3: Bring me a piece of the blue crystal on Kankāl's pillars, peopl. I want to cut to it.
folk.stage:runescribe.4: Guhamāt's stone is Under, where no born person will see its lines. Look at them for me.
folk.stage:runescribe.5: The second gate is a frame and remains, with no cut in it anywhere. I do not understand it.
folk.stage:runescribe.6: A line cut to the Ratan Crystal loses less than one cut to any crystal I have. Bring me a piece, peopl.
folk.stage:runescribe.7: Only the Cairn is left, peopl. The telling says it was the first stone, the one that covered most ground.
folk.stage:runescribe.8: If anyone sits at a great stone now the Cairn is open, tell me how its lines carry under the hand.
folk.stage:beastcaller.4: They call Guhamāt mother. It was a beast that dropped food, and small ones formed on the food.
folk.stage:beastcaller.5: Jīmūt never landed, so no hearth ever turned it. It was a beast like the rest.
folk.stage:beastcaller.6: Ratan was a beast bodied in crystal. By what you tell me, the small ones formed on its broken pieces.
folk.stage:beastcaller.7: Kuranga was the biggest of the pale beasts. That kind eats the other kinds.
folk.stage:beastcaller.8: What came up out of the Cairn was a beast bodied in Dressed Stone. It had eaten the stone it lay in.
folk.stage:deserter.3: Chandasāvak come up on the dark night now. At the fires they say the peopls did it.
folk.stage:deserter.4: You boiled Guhamāt down, peopl, and put its remains in a furnace. That furnace draws.
folk.stage:deserter.5: Your second gate is built round the flier's remains. Pull a piece from the frame while nobody is using it.
folk.stage:deserter.6: At the fires crystal is lees, and it goes in the fire. What you took off Ratan would be burned there.
folk.stage:deserter.7: Another of Kuranga's kind will come to its stones. At the fires they say a stone always draws one.
folk.stage:deserter.8: At the fires they say that heap was closed over a thing that could not be killed, and that the stones bred it.
It is dead now and the heap is open. They will want its remains burned.
folk.night:wayfinder: My hand is on the stone until first light, peopl. Ask me about the road in the morning.
Take what you need from the shelf and weigh the lees out yourself.
folk.night:provisioner: I am holding, peopl. Take what you want and set the lees down by the pot.
Bring your goods over here if you want to sell. I cannot get up before first light.
folk.night:smith: While I hold I cannot go to the anvil, peopl. Come back at first light.
Show me the bar by the lamp, and I will work it in the morning.
folk.night:apothecary: This hand stays on the stone tonight. I will see to your arm at first light.
On a quiet night like this my arm is only sore by morning.
folk.night:tinker: With one hand on the stone I cannot turn pieces over. Take what is laid out.
Come at first light and I will look at what you found.
folk.night:runescribe: The lines in this slab carry what my hand drives. I do not lift it until first light.
Ask me about cutting in the morning.
folk.night:beastcaller: Keep your small one out of this room tonight, peopl. Its bone is unsalted, and I am holding.
Buy what is out. The raw remains stay shut in their box until first light.
folk.night:deserter: I hold badly, peopl. My arm shakes long before first light.
Nobody taught me. I watched it done through walls I was sent to break.
folk.dark:wayfinder: It is Amāvassa, peopl. The moon is hollow tonight, and what was in it is on the ground.
Shut the door and stay off the open ground until the sun is up.
folk.dark:provisioner: No pack will come for the stores tonight. The things from the moon are out instead.
folk.dark:smith: The moon is dark, and my door stays shut until first light. Come in now or come in the morning.
folk.dark:apothecary: Chandasāvak cut deep, peopl. Come in and let me close it before you go out again.
folk.dark:tinker: No telling has the Chandasāvak coming up like this on a dark night.
folk.dark:runescribe: A lamp does nothing to the Chandasāvak once they are up, peopl. They give their own light.
folk.dark:beastcaller: The pale beasts are up to eat the other kinds, peopl. Tell me what you see them take.
folk.dark:deserter: On the sand we never saw a night like this.
At the fires tonight everyone is inside the light, and nobody sleeps.
folk.attack:wayfinder: I do not fight, peopl. Keep them off the bed while they are at the walls.
What has come is stronger than the lees in my pot.
folk.attack:provisioner: They have come for the stores. Get between them and the chests.
I do not fight, peopl. If they reach the bed I will have to go.
folk.attack:smith: Keep them off my anvil and the bed, peopl. I am holding and cannot lift the hammer.
A forge of remains draws as well as the chests. They will go for it.
folk.attack:apothecary: Stand at the edge, peopl. I am staying by the bed.
Bring me whoever is hurt when it is over.
folk.attack:tinker: They want what is in the chests. Do not let them have it.
My pieces are in the box by the bed. Keep them off it.
folk.attack:runescribe: No cut in any stone turns these. Fight them.
My hand stays on the slab. The edge is where you are needed.
folk.attack:beastcaller: Kill them at the edge, peopl. I do not fight.
There will be remains for the bone when it is done.
folk.attack:deserter: Whatever is out there has come for what draws.
If it is a march, they will not stop for me. I left them.
folk.idle:wayfinder: Where are you going next, peopl?
Have you cleared that Broken Store yet?
I can tell you which night the moon goes dark.
folk.idle:provisioner: I have meat and arrows if you are going out.
Somebody two hearths on is short of salt.
folk.idle:smith: Bring me ore I have not seen.
That edge needs a harder metal.
I work while it is light.
folk.idle:apothecary: Come back when the salve has done its work.
folk.idle:tinker: Show me what you are wearing.
folk.idle:runescribe: Have you stood at a great stone yet?
That crystal came out of deep rock.
folk.idle:beastcaller: Your small one is too near my pot.
Any nests where you have been?
I have Shade Flesh if you need more.
folk.idle:deserter: Do not set a chest of remains by my bed.
The fires are a long walk from here.
folk.buy:wayfinder: That came out of an old house on the road.
I carry the same on the road myself.
folk.buy:provisioner: That came three hearths to get here.
folk.buy:smith: I made it myself, at the anvil.
Keep the edge off stone harder than it is.
folk.buy:apothecary: Fruit, mushroom and fibre. Bind it over the cut.
folk.buy:tinker: I had that one from another walker.
Look after it. It is old work.
folk.buy:runescribe: Every line on it is my own cutting.
Do not knock the lines on it against stone.
folk.buy:beastcaller: Drive it once and a small one forms on the food.
Raw remains draw. Do not leave it lying in a store.
folk.buy:deserter: A march took that out of a store like yours.
It would not burn, so they left it in the sand.
folk.sell:wayfinder: Somebody down the road will want that.
It goes in my pack for the next hearth.
folk.sell:provisioner: Cheap, peopl. It has to be carried two hearths on.
There is a hearth on the road short of that.
folk.sell:smith: An iron piece can go back to the fire. A harder one cannot.
I pay for the metal in it.
folk.sell:apothecary: Fruit and caps go into the salves.
Mushrooms and fibre as well, if you have them.
folk.sell:tinker: Let me hold it a while before I weigh the lees.
Another walker will take it off me.
folk.sell:runescribe: Crystal from deep rock. I can cut to that.
folk.sell:beastcaller: Bone and raw remains are what I work with.
Bring me Shade Flesh after every dusk.
folk.sell:deserter: A walker will buy that off me for lees.
I pay little for it, peopl.
folk.short:wayfinder: Bring the rest of the lees, peopl, and it is yours.
folk.short:provisioner: You do not have the weight for that, peopl.
folk.short:smith: That does not cover the metal in it.
folk.short:apothecary: Not enough for the salve. Go and get the rest.
folk.short:tinker: Find a piece to sell me first. You cannot pay for that one.
folk.short:runescribe: Too little for what is cut into it.
folk.short:beastcaller: There is not enough lees in that.
folk.short:deserter: Beat off a march and you will have the Mūda for it.
folk.leave:wayfinder: You broke the bed, peopl. I will say why I left at the next hearth.
folk.leave:provisioner: There is nothing to sit on through the night. I am taking my goods down the road.
folk.leave:smith: I cannot hold here without a bed, peopl. I will sit down at an old house tonight.
folk.leave:apothecary: Someone broke my bed. I will see to holders' arms at another hearth.
folk.leave:tinker: I am going, with nowhere to hold. The walkers will hear of your Joining Bench.
folk.leave:runescribe: A holder needs a seat for the night, and mine is broken. I am leaving.
folk.leave:beastcaller: My bed is broken, peopl. I am packing the bone and going.
folk.leave:deserter: The bed is gone, and no fire will take me. I will find an empty house to hold in.
folk.extra:deserter.burrower: The burrower took our people while we lived on its sand. They were in it when you boiled it down.
folk.extra:wayfinder.moon_in: Amāvassa is in {n} nights, peopl. Be under a roof or where you mean to fight.
folk.extra:wayfinder.moon_in_one: Amāvassa is tomorrow night. Have a roof over you by dusk.
folk.extra:wayfinder.moon_tonight: Amāvassa is tonight. The moon is hollow, and the Chandasāvak have come down with its slivers.
walker.say:dusk: I sit at this well until dark, peopl. Then I take my pot into the nearest house and hold it.
The crate in the end house has food in it. Fill it again when you pass.
I walk by day and sit down in whatever old house I reach by dusk.
Two pots this close would bring a pack, so I am the only one here.
Holders on this road would sit down under your roof, peopl, if it had a bed, a door and a light.
At dark my hand goes on the stone, and it stays there until first light.
walker.say:dark: It is Amāvassa, peopl. I am inside with the door shut.
The moon is hollow tonight. Get under a roof.
walker.say:raid: Packs are out for the stores tonight, and my pot is a store too.
Keep away from this house tonight, peopl. A pack that follows you here will cross my pot.
fire.say:before: Nothing comes up on this sand but the burrower's own, peopl. Do not bring a store onto it.
There is nothing here for you.
fire.say:after: You killed the burrower. The sand is open now.
Nothing of ours draws. Go back to your stores.
fire.say:night: Stay inside the light, peopl, where nothing comes up.
Stand where we can see you, and keep your hands off the fire.
fire.say:struck: Drive it out of the light. It will get up somewhere else.
You broke the ground of our fire, peopl. We will drive you off it.
fire.say:fuel: Leave the wood at the edge and go.
Coal burns longer. Set it down and step back.
The fire takes it. You get no place inside the light for it.
march.say:march: Find the lees. It goes to the fire.
Cut the peopl down and get to the chests.
Every store here draws. Burn it.
The bed it comes back to draws too. Break it.
Back inside the light before dusk.
march.say:beaten: Drop what you carry and walk.
Dusk is coming. Back to the fire.
